paragraphs.text: Your objectives remain unchanged from the last review: you are seeking long-term growth, and do not require any income from your portfolio for the foreseeable future. Both of you are currently at a moderate risk level and are comfortable maintaining this position.
Your recorded risk profile is {{value-1}} moderate.
Jean has received an inheritance of around {{value-1}} from her late mother's estate. These funds have now cleared and you wish to invest this alongside your existing portfolio.
The recommended source of funds is the inheritance received by Jean and the joint General Investment Account.
The recommended approach is to use the inheritance of GBP {{value-1}} together with the full value of the joint GIA.
We recommend making ISA top-ups for both of you for the new tax year and opening a new joint investment account with the remaining funds.
This recommendation involves selling your existing investments within the joint GIA.

The plan we agreed is to disinvest the joint GIA and, together with the inheritance, fund both Robert's and Jean's ISAs for the new tax year and open a new jointly-held investment account for the balance.
Selling down the GIA is a disposal, so there is a capital gains position to consider in this report. This may create a capital gains tax liability, to be assessed against the annual exempt amount.
